messages.content: What is AI engineering?

The technical field of designing, building, evaluating, and operating useful applications and systems using pretrained foundation models (mainly LLMs) as components. It focuses on selecting models, connecting them to data and tools, and iterating on evaluation and improvement, rather than building models from scratch.
Briefly explain AI engineering.

The technical field of designing, building, evaluating, and operating useful applications and systems using pretrained foundation models (mainly LLMs) as components. It focuses on selecting models, connecting them to data and tools, and iterating on evaluation and improvement, rather than building models from scratch.
What is Evaluation and improvement cycle?

A development approach that repeats build → measure → improve. Since AI application outputs vary probabilistically, judge quality using evaluation data and metrics rather than intuition, then improve prompts, data, models, and tools based on the results. In this course, we repeat this cycle across lectures using a learning support agent.
Briefly explain Evaluation and improvement cycle.

What is LLM (Large Language Model)?

A model trained on large amounts of text that generates text by predicting the tokens following its input. It can handle many tasks, including question answering, summarization, and code generation, simply by changing the instructions (prompt).
Briefly explain LLM (Large Language Model).

A model trained on large amounts of text that generates text by predicting the tokens following its input. It can handle many tasks, including question answering, summarization, and code generation, simply by changing the instructions (prompt).
What is Token?

The smallest unit an LLM uses to process text. Text is split into fragments of words or characters. API charges, rate limits, and context window sizes are often counted in tokens. Tokenization varies by language; for example, Japanese tends to require more tokens per character than English.
Briefly explain Token.

What is Context window?

The maximum total number of input and output tokens an LLM can handle in one call. Conversation history and tool results must also fit within this limit, making the choice of what to pass to the model important.
Briefly explain Context window.

The maximum total number of input and output tokens an LLM can handle in one call. Conversation history and tool results must also fit within this limit, making the choice of what to pass to the model important.
What is Prompt?
Input text passed to an LLM. In addition to questions, it can include roles, constraints, output formats, and examples to guide the output.
Briefly explain Prompt.
Input text passed to an LLM. In addition to questions, it can include roles, constraints, output formats, and examples to guide the output.
What is System prompt?
Input that specifies model behavior (role, tone, rules, and so on) separately from the user's question. In Pydantic AI, it is provided through the Agent instructions argument.
Briefly explain System prompt.
Input that specifies model behavior (role, tone, rules, and so on) separately from the user's question. In Pydantic AI, it is provided through the Agent instructions argument.
What is temperature?

A setting that adjusts randomness when choosing the next token. Lower values make outputs more stable; higher values make them more varied. This is one reason the same question can yield different answers.
Briefly explain temperature.

A setting that adjusts randomness when choosing the next token. Lower values make outputs more stable; higher values make them more varied. This is one reason the same question can yield different answers.
What is Hallucination?

The phenomenon of an LLM generating plausible content that is factually incorrect or nonexistent. It is more likely when asked about things the model does not know, such as recent information or organization- or course-specific details. Mitigations include consulting external data through tools, asking for evidence, and detecting errors through evaluation.
Briefly explain Hallucination.

What is API?
An interface through which a program calls the functionality of another service. In this course, we use an LLM by calling the Gemini API from Python.
Briefly explain API.
An interface through which a program calls the functionality of another service. In this course, we use an LLM by calling the Gemini API from Python.
What is API key?

A secret string that identifies the person calling an API. If it leaks, someone else can consume your usage allowance, so do not put it directly in code, commit it, or paste it into chat. In this course, register it as a Codespaces secret and read it through the GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable.
Briefly explain API key.

A secret string that identifies the person calling an API. If it leaks, someone else can consume your usage allowance, so do not put it directly in code, commit it, or paste it into chat. In this course, register it as a Codespaces secret and read it through the GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable.
What is Environment variable?
A value set outside a program (in the OS or execution environment) that the program can read by name. Used to separate secrets such as API keys and environment-specific settings from code.
Briefly explain Environment variable.
A value set outside a program (in the OS or execution environment) that the program can read by name. Used to separate secrets such as API keys and environment-specific settings from code.
What is Rate limit?

A limit on requests or tokens within a given time period. Exceeding it returns errors such as HTTP 429. Free tiers have particularly strict limits, and agents reach them easily because they call the LLM multiple times for one question.
Briefly explain Rate limit.

A limit on requests or tokens within a given time period. Exceeding it returns errors such as HTTP 429. Free tiers have particularly strict limits, and agents reach them easily because they call the LLM multiple times for one question.
What is GitHub Codespaces?

A cloud development environment provided by GitHub. Open VS Code in a browser and immediately use an environment configured by the repository. Personal accounts have a monthly free allowance; if you do not stop the Codespace when idle, it continues consuming that allowance.
Briefly explain GitHub Codespaces.

A cloud development environment provided by GitHub. Open VS Code in a browser and immediately use an environment configured by the repository. Personal accounts have a monthly free allowance; if you do not stop the Codespace when idle, it continues consuming that allowance.
What is devcontainer?

A mechanism for defining a development environment as a container. Specify the Python version, extensions, and startup commands in .devcontainer/devcontainer.json so everyone opening Codespaces gets the same environment.
Briefly explain devcontainer.

A mechanism for defining a development environment as a container. Specify the Python version, extensions, and startup commands in .devcontainer/devcontainer.json so everyone opening Codespaces gets the same environment.
What is Codespaces secret?

A secret value registered in your GitHub account settings. It is passed as an environment variable when you start Codespaces for a selected repository. When registering it, select the repository you will use (your own fork). If registered while a Codespace is running, restart the Codespace.
Briefly explain Codespaces secret.

A secret value registered in your GitHub account settings. It is passed as an environment variable when you start Codespaces for a selected repository. When registering it, select the repository you will use (your own fork). If registered while a Codespace is running, restart the Codespace.
What is fork?
Copying someone else's entire repository to your own account. In this course, fork the course repository and work and submit within your own fork.
Briefly explain fork.
Copying someone else's entire repository to your own account. In this course, fork the course repository and work and submit within your own fork.
What is Branch?

A mechanism for separating streams of work. Try changes without breaking main, then merge them into main through a PR once ready. In this course, create a working branch such as lec01 for each lecture.
Briefly explain Branch.

A mechanism for separating streams of work. Try changes without breaking main, then merge them into main through a PR once ready. In this course, create a working branch such as lec01 for each lecture.
What is Pull Request (PR)?

A mechanism for requesting that changes from one branch be merged into another. It supports reviewing differences, comments, and displaying automated test results. Submit work for this course as a PR from your working branch to main within your own fork.
Briefly explain Pull Request (PR).

A mechanism for requesting that changes from one branch be merged into another. It supports reviewing differences, comments, and displaying automated test results. Submit work for this course as a PR from your working branch to main within your own fork.
What is GitHub Copilot?
GitHub's AI coding assistance. It supports code completion in the editor, questions in chat, and editing multiple files in Agent mode. Copilot Free limits completion counts and chat usage.
Briefly explain GitHub Copilot.
GitHub's AI coding assistance. It supports code completion in the editor, questions in chat, and editing multiple files in Agent mode. Copilot Free limits completion counts and chat usage.
What is Code completion?

A feature in which AI suggests code to follow partially written code or comments. Accept suggestions with Tab or a similar action. Suggestions may be incorrect, so read and understand them before accepting.
Briefly explain Code completion.

A feature in which AI suggests code to follow partially written code or comments. Accept suggestions with Tab or a similar action. Suggestions may be incorrect, so read and understand them before accepting.
What is Coding agent?

AI that autonomously carries out requested programming work over multiple steps, using tools to read and write files and run commands. Examples include Claude Code, Copilot Agent mode, and Pi. Internally, it has the same LLM + loop + tools structure as an AI agent.
Briefly explain Coding agent.

AI that autonomously carries out requested programming work over multiple steps, using tools to read and write files and run commands. Examples include Claude Code, Copilot Agent mode, and Pi. Internally, it has the same LLM + loop + tools structure as an AI agent.
What is Pretraining?
The initial stage of training a model to predict the next token using large amounts of general-purpose text. Much of its language knowledge and general common sense is acquired here.
Briefly explain Pretraining.
The initial stage of training a model to predict the next token using large amounts of general-purpose text. Much of its language knowledge and general common sense is acquired here.
What is Fine-tuning?

Further training a pretrained model on data suited to a specific task or format. It is suitable for teaching output format, tone, or behavior in a specific domain. For up-to-date facts, consulting external data through tools or RAG is often more suitable.
Briefly explain Fine-tuning.

Further training a pretrained model on data suited to a specific task or format. It is suitable for teaching output format, tone, or behavior in a specific domain. For up-to-date facts, consulting external data through tools or RAG is often more suitable.
What is Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)?
A method of further training a model using pairs of inputs and desired outputs, such as questions and model answers. A representative method for teaching instruction-following behavior.
Briefly explain Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT).
A method of further training a model using pairs of inputs and desired outputs, such as questions and model answers. A representative method for teaching instruction-following behavior.
What is PEFT?

An umbrella term for methods that train only a small subset of model parameters or a small set of added parameters instead of all parameters. This can greatly reduce GPU memory and storage requirements. LoRA is a representative example.
Briefly explain PEFT.

An umbrella term for methods that train only a small subset of model parameters or a small set of added parameters instead of all parameters. This can greatly reduce GPU memory and storage requirements. LoRA is a representative example.
What is LoRA?

A PEFT method that freezes pretrained weights, represents weight updates as the product of two small matrices (low-rank matrices), and trains only those small matrices. It trains few parameters and saves the results (adapters) in small files. The Lecture 02 exercises cover LoRA.
Briefly explain LoRA.

A PEFT method that freezes pretrained weights, represents weight updates as the product of two small matrices (low-rank matrices), and trains only those small matrices. It trains few parameters and saves the results (adapters) in small files. The Lecture 02 exercises cover LoRA.
What is Rank (LoRA r)?
A hyperparameter that determines the size of the low-rank matrices used in LoRA. A larger value increases expressive capacity, but also increases the number of trainable parameters and memory use.
Briefly explain Rank (LoRA r).
A hyperparameter that determines the size of the low-rank matrices used in LoRA. A larger value increases expressive capacity, but also increases the number of trainable parameters and memory use.
What is QLoRA?

A method that saves memory by quantizing base-model weights to, for example, 4 bits, then trains with LoRA. This lets smaller GPUs handle larger models. In the Lecture 02 exercises, the model fits in GPU memory, so we train with LoRA and compare memory and output differences when loading in 4-bit in the advanced section.
Briefly explain QLoRA.

A method that saves memory by quantizing base-model weights to, for example, 4 bits, then trains with LoRA. This lets smaller GPUs handle larger models. In the Lecture 02 exercises, the model fits in GPU memory, so we train with LoRA and compare memory and output differences when loading in 4-bit in the advanced section.
What is Quantization?
A technique for representing model weights with fewer bits (for example, from 16 bits to 4 bits) to reduce memory use and computation. Accuracy may decrease slightly.
Briefly explain Quantization.
A technique for representing model weights with fewer bits (for example, from 16 bits to 4 bits) to reduce memory use and computation. Accuracy may decrease slightly.
What is Learning rate?
A hyperparameter that determines how far parameters move in one update. Too large a value makes training unstable; too small a value slows progress.
Briefly explain Learning rate.
A hyperparameter that determines how far parameters move in one update. Too large a value makes training unstable; too small a value slows progress.
What is Epoch?
One pass through the entire training dataset is one epoch. Too many epochs can cause overfitting.
Briefly explain Epoch.
One pass through the entire training dataset is one epoch. Too many epochs can cause overfitting.
What is Overfitting?
A state in which the model fits training data excessively and performs worse on unseen inputs. Detect it by measuring performance on validation data not used for training.
Briefly explain Overfitting.
A state in which the model fits training data excessively and performs worse on unseen inputs. Detect it by measuring performance on validation data not used for training.
What is Hugging Face Hub?
A platform for sharing and downloading public models and datasets. Used to obtain open-weight models and publish LoRA adapters.
Briefly explain Hugging Face Hub.
A platform for sharing and downloading public models and datasets. Used to obtain open-weight models and publish LoRA adapters.
What is AI agent?
A system that achieves a goal through a loop in which an LLM decides to call tools, examines the results, and decides its next action. Its basic structure is "model + loop + tools".
Briefly explain AI agent.
A system that achieves a goal through a loop in which an LLM decides to call tools, examines the results, and decides its next action. Its basic structure is "model + loop + tools".
What is Agent loop?

The process of passing input to the model → executing any tool calls returned by the model → returning results to the model, repeated until the model gives a final answer. Multiple LLM calls for one question have a substantial effect on time, charges, and rate limits.
Briefly explain Agent loop.

The process of passing input to the model → executing any tool calls returned by the model → returning results to the model, repeated until the model gives a final answer. Multiple LLM calls for one question have a substantial effect on time, charges, and rate limits.
What is Tool (Tool use / Function calling)?

A function made available for the model to call. The model looks at its name, description, and argument types, chooses arguments when needed, and requests a call; the program executes it. Used for search, calculations, file operations, external API calls, and more.
Briefly explain Tool (Tool use / Function calling).

A function made available for the model to call. The model looks at its name, description, and argument types, chooses arguments when needed, and requests a call; the program executes it. Used for search, calculations, file operations, external API calls, and more.
What is Tool description?

Text that explains a tool's purpose and argument meanings to the model. In Pydantic AI, it is generated automatically from the function docstring and type hints. Since the model reads it to decide whether and how to call a tool, its wording can greatly affect behavior.
Briefly explain Tool description.

Text that explains a tool's purpose and argument meanings to the model. In Pydantic AI, it is generated automatically from the function docstring and type hints. Since the model reads it to decide whether and how to call a tool, its wording can greatly affect behavior.
What is Structured output?
A mechanism for receiving model outputs according to specified types or a JSON schema. This makes programmatic postprocessing easier. In Pydantic AI, specify a Pydantic model in output_type.
Briefly explain Structured output.
A mechanism for receiving model outputs according to specified types or a JSON schema. This makes programmatic postprocessing easier. In Pydantic AI, specify a Pydantic model in output_type.
What is Harness?

A program that surrounds an LLM with a loop, tools, a user interface (UI), and so on to enable actual work. Claude Code and Pi are examples. Pi is known as a thin harness with just four built-in tools: read, write, edit, and bash.
Briefly explain Harness.

A program that surrounds an LLM with a loop, tools, a user interface (UI), and so on to enable actual work. Claude Code and Pi are examples. Pi is known as a thin harness with just four built-in tools: read, write, edit, and bash.
What is Pi?

An open-source (MIT-licensed) coding agent that runs in the terminal. It has minimal features and a minimal system prompt, designed for users to extend. Version 1.0 was released in October 2026. Its npm package name is @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.
Briefly explain Pi.

An open-source (MIT-licensed) coding agent that runs in the terminal. It has minimal features and a minimal system prompt, designed for users to extend. Version 1.0 was released in October 2026. Its npm package name is @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.
What is Pydantic AI?

A framework for building agents in Python. It uses Pydantic types to define tool arguments and outputs and handles many models, such as Gemini and OpenAI, with the same code style. Test models let you check behavior without API calls. It is the main framework for Lecture 03.
Briefly explain Pydantic AI.

A framework for building agents in Python. It uses Pydantic types to define tool arguments and outputs and handles many models, such as Gemini and OpenAI, with the same code style. Test models let you check behavior without API calls. It is the main framework for Lecture 03.
What is ADK (Agent Development Kit)?

An open-source agent development framework released by Google. It integrates closely with Gemini, and adk web lets you visually follow tool calls. Version 2.0 introduces breaking changes from the 1.x series. This course covers it in the Advanced homework.
Briefly explain ADK (Agent Development Kit).

An open-source agent development framework released by Google. It integrates closely with Gemini, and adk web lets you visually follow tool calls. Version 2.0 introduces breaking changes from the 1.x series. This course covers it in the Advanced homework.
What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?

An open standard protocol connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources. Tools exposed through an MCP server can be used in a common way from compatible agents and editors (MCP clients). In Lecture 05, you will experience this by turning glossary search into an MCP server.
Briefly explain MCP (Model Context Protocol).

An open standard protocol connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources. Tools exposed through an MCP server can be used in a common way from compatible agents and editors (MCP clients). In Lecture 05, you will experience this by turning glossary search into an MCP server.
What is Guardrail?

A constraint or check designed to prevent undesirable agent behavior or outputs. Methods include rules in instructions, restricting tool permissions, checking outputs, and requesting human confirmation before important operations.
Briefly explain Guardrail.

A constraint or check designed to prevent undesirable agent behavior or outputs. Methods include rules in instructions, restricting tool permissions, checking outputs, and requesting human confirmation before important operations.
What is Human-in-the-loop?

Incorporating human confirmation or approval into agent processing. Used before operations that are difficult to undo, such as writing or sending data. In Pydantic AI, tools with requires_approval=True support this.
Briefly explain Human-in-the-loop.

Incorporating human confirmation or approval into agent processing. Used before operations that are difficult to undo, such as writing or sending data. In Pydantic AI, tools with requires_approval=True support this.
What is TestModel?

A fake model included in Pydantic AI for testing. It calls tools and returns dummy answers without calling a real LLM. It lets you test agent wiring (whether tools are registered, called, and return results) without an API key or usage allowance.
Briefly explain TestModel.

A fake model included in Pydantic AI for testing. It calls tools and returns dummy answers without calling a real LLM. It lets you test agent wiring (whether tools are registered, called, and return results) without an API key or usage allowance.
What is 3 homework levels?

The structure of AIE2026 homework. There are three levels: "Basic (review lecture content)", "Implementation (write your own code)", and "Advanced (research and experimentation)". Completing any one level completes the homework for that lecture. As a rule, it is not graded.
Briefly explain 3 homework levels.

The structure of AIE2026 homework. There are three levels: "Basic (review lecture content)", "Implementation (write your own code)", and "Advanced (research and experimentation)". Completing any one level completes the homework for that lecture. As a rule, it is not graded.
What is answer.md?

The file for recording exercise and homework results for each AIE2026 lecture. Located at lectures/NN/answer.md. Record the level attempted, what you did, results, and observations, then submit by opening a PR from your working branch to main in your own fork.
Briefly explain answer.md.

The file for recording exercise and homework results for each AIE2026 lecture. Located at lectures/NN/answer.md. Record the level attempted, what you did, results, and observations, then submit by opening a PR from your working branch to main in your own fork.
What is lecNN-start tag?

A Git tag on the starting code for each lecture's exercises in the AIE2026 course repository (for example, lec03-start). Even if you have not finished the previous lecture, creating a branch from this tag lets you start the current lecture's exercises.
Briefly explain lecNN-start tag.

A Git tag on the starting code for each lecture's exercises in the AIE2026 course repository (for example, lec03-start). Even if you have not finished the previous lecture, creating a branch from this tag lets you start the current lecture's exercises.
What is Default model?

The standard model for AIE2026 exercises and homework is gemini-3.5-flash-lite, chosen with free-tier rate limits and stable course operation in mind. You may switch models with the AIE_MODEL environment variable or use your own API subscription.
Briefly explain Default model.

The standard model for AIE2026 exercises and homework is gemini-3.5-flash-lite, chosen with free-tier rate limits and stable course operation in mind. You may switch models with the AIE_MODEL environment variable or use your own API subscription.
What is External tool?

Using capabilities outside the agent program, such as web retrieval, file operations, databases, and third-party APIs, as tools. Lecture 03 function tools run within the same process, whereas external tools are called across processes or machines. MCP is a common protocol for this.
Briefly explain External tool.

Using capabilities outside the agent program, such as web retrieval, file operations, databases, and third-party APIs, as tools. Lecture 03 function tools run within the same process, whereas external tools are called across processes or machines. MCP is a common protocol for this.
What is MCP server?

The program that exposes tools (and resources or prompts) through MCP. It exposes tool names, descriptions, and argument schemas, executes tools in response to client requests, and returns results. In this course, glossary search becomes an MCP server (app/mcp_server.py). Many ready-made servers are available, including fetch, filesystem, and GitHub.
Briefly explain MCP server.

The program that exposes tools (and resources or prompts) through MCP. It exposes tool names, descriptions, and argument schemas, executes tools in response to client requests, and returns results. In this course, glossary search becomes an MCP server (app/mcp_server.py). Many ready-made servers are available, including fetch, filesystem, and GitHub.
What is MCP client?

The component that connects to MCP servers, passes their tools to the model, and calls tools as directed by the model. Agent programs (Pydantic AI's MCPToolset) and editors or applications such as Copilot Chat, Claude Desktop, and Cursor can serve as clients. A benefit of MCP is using the same server from different clients.
Briefly explain MCP client.

The component that connects to MCP servers, passes their tools to the model, and calls tools as directed by the model. Agent programs (Pydantic AI's MCPToolset) and editors or applications such as Copilot Chat, Claude Desktop, and Cursor can serve as clients. A benefit of MCP is using the same server from different clients.
What is Transport (stdio / Streamable HTTP)?

The communication channel between an MCP client and server. With stdio, the client starts the server as a subprocess and exchanges messages through standard input/output (simple and used on the same machine). With Streamable HTTP, the server listens at a URL, allowing connections from other processes or machines (access scope and authentication must be considered).
Briefly explain Transport (stdio / Streamable HTTP).

The communication channel between an MCP client and server. With stdio, the client starts the server as a subprocess and exchanges messages through standard input/output (simple and used on the same machine). With Streamable HTTP, the server listens at a URL, allowing connections from other processes or machines (access scope and authentication must be considered).
What is mcpServers configuration?

A configuration file listing MCP servers to use. For each server, specify a name and a startup command (stdio) or destination URL (HTTP). Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Pydantic AI read the same mcpServers format (VS Code / Copilot Chat uses servers). This course uses app/mcp_servers.json. Adding tools with just a few configuration lines is central to the MCP experience.
Briefly explain mcpServers configuration.

A configuration file listing MCP servers to use. For each server, specify a name and a startup command (stdio) or destination URL (HTTP). Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Pydantic AI read the same mcpServers format (VS Code / Copilot Chat uses servers). This course uses app/mcp_servers.json. Adding tools with just a few configuration lines is central to the MCP experience.
What is Tool namespace?

Adding a prefix such as "server_name_tool_name" to distinguish identically named tools when using multiple MCP servers. This course's app/agent.py automatically adds the server name from the configuration (for example, glossary_search_glossary; Pydantic AI's load_mcp_toolsets does the same). More tools mean more descriptions sent to the model, affecting tool-selection accuracy and token counts.
Briefly explain Tool namespace.

Adding a prefix such as "server_name_tool_name" to distinguish identically named tools when using multiple MCP servers. This course's app/agent.py automatically adds the server name from the configuration (for example, glossary_search_glossary; Pydantic AI's load_mcp_toolsets does the same). More tools mean more descriptions sent to the model, affecting tool-selection accuracy and token counts.
What is fetch server?

A ready-made MCP server that retrieves a specified URL and returns the page body as Markdown (written in Python; started with uvx mcp-server-fetch). This course uses it as an example of "adding an external tool just through configuration". It actually accesses URLs chosen by the model, so users must understand where it sends data and what it sends.
Briefly explain fetch server.

A ready-made MCP server that retrieves a specified URL and returns the page body as Markdown (written in Python; started with uvx mcp-server-fetch).
